To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a cancer stem cell has been identified in human brain tumors that is responsible for tumor initiation and maintenance.
a cancer stem cell can be isolated from human brain tumors and this cancer stem cell has the capacity to proliferate and self renew.

1) we isolated and characterized a cancer stem cell (BTCS) from human brain tumors; 2) the BTCS possesses a marked proliferative and self-renewal potential; 3) the BTSC is the origin of the tumor clone and is responsible for maintaining the heterogeneity of brain tumors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the cancer stem cell and the development of new therapies to eradicate it.
the molecular and cellular characterization of a brain tumor stem cell.
the development of novel approaches to the treatment of brain tumors, which are based on the identification and isolation of a cancer stem cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CD133+ cells from the human brain tumor samples are capable of forming tumors in the brain, are self renewing and can differentiate into tumor cells of various phenotypes.
CD133+ cells are the cancer stem cells in human brain tumors.
the BTSC is a cell with extensive self-renewal potential, capable of differentiating into the major cell types found within the tumor, and is responsible for the maintenance of the tumor clone.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have identified a cancer stem cell (CSC) that is responsible for maintaining the bulk tumor mass in human brain tumors, and that this CSC is exclusively isolated in the fraction of cells expressing the neural stem/progenitor cell surface marker CD 133.
we have identified a cancer stem cell that is the origin of human brain tumors.

we have identified a cancer stem cell (or tumor initiating cell) in human brain tumors that is a rare population of cells that possess the capacity for proliferation, differentiation, and self renewal.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the tumor clone in the brain is organized as a hierarchical stem cell structure.
there is a stem cell population within brain tumors, which is responsible for maintaining the tumour mass.
the cancer stem cell is not a rare cell in human brain tumor.
